ledger_conventions.pl_rounding: Each play settles to a 2-decimal P/L (American-odds payout rounded at settlement). Running units = sum of these rounded per-play values, so the ledger column sums EXACTLY to the total (sportsbook-settlement convention, chosen for auditability). Note: summing unrounded payouts can differ by ~0.01u (e.g. baseline 7/23 is +0.48u rounded, +0.49u unrounded).
ledger_conventions.brier_ab: raw-vs-shrunk Brier/logloss compared only on plays where BOTH probabilities exist (engine skips produce no shrunk_p). 7/23 n_both=4 (Dobnak excluded).
ledger_conventions.objective: profitability = EV vs price break-even, NOT win% > 50%.

decision_policy_version.definition: The whole decision path a play passes through: projector + selector thresholds + intake guards + settlement maths. A change to ANY of them starts a new version, because the plays the new path produces are not exchangeable with the plays the old one produced.

components.projector: engine.kprops proj(): START-ONLY accumulation; K-rate prior 0.22 at 80 TBF; E[TBF] prior 24.0 at 3 starts; returns nothing below 5 GS
components.selector: engine.kprops select_play(): EV>0; edge>=0.04 against the conditional-on-settling probability p/(1-p_push); |proj-line|>=0.8; side==sign(disp); weight 0.5 if GS<10
components.intake_guards: short-line hold: any arm posted at <=3.5 K is rejected without --allow-short-lines (added 2026-07-27, lineage b23c254)
components.settlement: probs(ek,line) -> (p_over, p_push, p_under); ev() three-outcome (added 2026-07-27, commit 91d2d9c)

experiment_queue.title: HR log-odds shrinkage in a log5 event model
experiment_queue.id_note: Takes E6, not E5: 'E4' is already assigned twice in this queue (lineup-aware offense; V13-vs-moneyline). That pre-existing collision is NOT resolved here, only avoided.
experiment_queue.method: log5 in odds form odds(b)*odds(p)/odds(L) [exact identity, not an approximation], then HR shrunk toward league by weighted geometric interpolation in odds space: odds(h)=odds(q_HR)^(1-s)*odds(L_HR)^s, equivalently h=logistic((1-s)*logit(q_HR)+s*logit(L_HR)). Normalisation scheme PRE-COMMITTED to A (ANCHOR_HR): P(HR)=h; P(e)=(1-h)*raw[e]/sum_{j!=HR} raw[j].
corrections_superseding_prior_claims: WITHDRAWN: 'log-odds interpolation is less violent at the extremes than probability interpolation.' NOT universal. True when both endpoints sit near the same boundary (0.001->0.030 at s=0.5 gives 0.00553 vs linear 0.01550); FALSE when endpoints are far apart in log-odds space (0.500->0.001 gives 0.03067 vs linear 0.25050, an 8x difference). REPLACED BY the three defensible properties: bounded, preserves endpoints, interpolates geometrically in odds space.

STRENGTHENED: independent binary log5 over mutually exclusive events generally does NOT sum to one (structural; holds even when b, p and L each sum to 1). Dividing every event by sum(raw) rescales HR too, so the delivered HR rate is NOT the value the shrinkage formula produced. The consequence is interpretive: the direct binary-logit interpretation of hr_shrink does not survive downstream normalisation. The parameter could still be estimated end-to-end against the final normalised distribution, but it would no longer mean the stated interpolation weight. Normalisation changes interpretation; it does not by itself demonstrate statistical non-identifiability. Illustrative synthetic case: sum(raw)=0.992512, h=0.036381, post-renormalisation 0.036655, drift +0.75% relative. Magnitude is data-dependent; the defect is not.
blocking_prereqs_before_hr_shrink_may_be: 1. Are b and p already regressed? Double shrinkage gives total pull 1-(1-w1)(1-s), not s. Deliverable: the prior weight already embedded in each input.

2. Is HR modelled per PA or conditional on BBE? BBE is the sample size for HR|BBE; if HR is per PA the sample size is PA and BBE mixes units. If truly conditional, the distribution must be P(BBE)*P(HR|BBE), which the reviewed code does not do.
3. How are hitter and pitcher sample uncertainty combined? One scalar cannot represent two independent sample sizes. Either shrink b and p separately, or state and justify the combination rule.

4. Is the target sampling uncertainty or calibration correction? Sampling -> K/(n+K), decays with n, K from a variance decomposition. Calibration -> a fitted slope that does NOT decay with n and belongs in a calibration layer. One parameter fitted to outcomes absorbs both and will not generalise.
guards: assert 0.0 <= hr_shrink <= 1.0 -- outside [0,1] the geometric interpolation EXTRAPOLATES (s>1 overshoots past L, s<0 pushes away); K/(n+K) is in range only if K>=0 and n>=0, and a NaN or missing n breaks it silently

clip b[e], p[e], L[e] to [1e-6, 1-1e-6] BEFORE _odds(): _odds(p)=p/(1-p) is undefined at p=1, and _odds(L[e]) sits in a DENOMINATOR so L[e]=0 (plausible for 3B early in a season) breaks. Exact boundary probabilities can produce division by zero, infinity or NaN depending on scalar versus array arithmetic and subsequent operations. The REQUIRED INVARIANT is finite output after clipping -- every intermediate and every output finite, with any non-finite value a hard failure -- not a specific predicted failure mode. A non-finite raw[e] also contaminates sum(raw), so the blast radius is not confined to the offending event.

known_issues.text: The observed residual-line correlation is mechanically contaminated by shared-variable coupling and projection compression; it is not an admissible edge metric.
known_issues.identity: corr(R,L) = (rho_XL*sigma_X - sigma_L)/sqrt(sigma_X^2 + sigma_L^2 - 2*rho_XL*sigma_X*sigma_L), R = X - L. Equivalently cov(R,L) = (beta_X~L - 1)*var(L); beta < 1 mechanically makes residuals negatively associated with line height. 2026-07-27 board (n=23): sigma_X 0.8504, sigma_L 1.0170, rho_XL 0.7916, beta 0.6620, corr(R,L) -0.5518.
known_issues.correction: WITHDRAWN: 'the dispersion gap alone predicts -0.5518'. sigma_X < sigma_L alone does NOT pin corr(R,L); the identity requires all three moments including the observed rho_XL. Inserting observed board moments and recovering the observed correlation is an IN-SAMPLE ALGEBRAIC RECONSTRUCTION, not independent evidence that under-dispersion caused the relationship.
known_issues.does_not_establish: That the projection contains no incremental information. A compressed estimator can still carry real signal. The coupling makes corr(R,L) inadmissible as a metric; it does not adjudicate the underlying question. Resolution requires the after-outcomes tests, not this diagnostic.

WITHDRAWN: 'market 3.5 implies approximately 15 batters faced'. A strikeout line reflects the market's JOINT expectation over workload, K-rate, outcome distribution and pricing. TBF cannot be uniquely recovered from a line without separately specifying a market K-rate and a probability model. The underlying concern (KPROP-OPENER-2: E[TBF] may not read what a low line signals) is unaffected and stands.

Does the projection add information BEYOND the market? (1) compare an outcome model using market line + two-sided prices against one adding E[K]; (2) orthogonalise U = E[K] - fitted_E[K](market information); (3) test whether U predicts actual K minus the market forecast; (4) compare held-out MAE and NLL, NOT residual-vs-line correlation (inadmissible per KPROP-EDGE-ARTIFACT); (5) n~23 is EXPLORATORY, no verdict moves on it. Use a PRICE-ADJUSTED market forecast where complete two-sided prices exist -- a half-point line alone is only a coarse market estimate.

calibration_2026_07_25_oos.status: EXPLORATORY - one slate, n=24, not pre-registered, NOT confirmatory
calibration_2026_07_25_oos.finding: Point projections are UNDER-DISPERSED: projected sd 0.96 against actual sd 2.67, OLS slope 1.35. The shrinkage is too aggressive - the fix would be to stretch the projections, not to shift them. BUT the quantity K-props actually price is the Poisson TAIL, and the tails came in close to nominal (6 vs 4.5 expected at SO>=8, 5 vs 5.8 at SO<=3), because Poisson noise supplies most of the missing dispersion. So this slate is evidence of a real but modest defect in the point estimate and NOT evidence that prop pricing is broken.
calibration_2026_07_25_oos.caveat: n=24 on ONE slate. The slope CI is wide enough to include 1.0. This does not license an engine change; it licenses a pre-registered experiment (R7).

integrity_tests.T1_hold: PASS - 31/31 two-sided quotes inside the 2-12% band, zero out of band.
integrity_tests.T2_rung_coherence: PASS - 0 rows with an incoherent ladder.
integrity_tests.T2_caveat: T2 is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and this board proves it. Misiorowski's ladder (12.5@-135 / 11.5@-330) is perfectly rung-coherent and is still not a usable main line: OVER 12.5 K at -135 does not exist as a starter market. A coherent ladder can be an alt-line ladder. Do not treat T2 as a pass to price.
integrity_tests.T3_dispersion: 10 of 30 rows QUARANTINED for cross-book line spread > 1.0 K.
integrity_tests.T3_is_the_discriminator: Dispersion, not hold and not rung coherence, is what separates a book's main line from an alt rung on an aggregator display.
integrity_tests.T4_independent_reread: PASS - the 4 rows transcribed in the live pass re-read identically from a fresh crop, 0 disagreements.

engine_vs_market_shrinkage.design: OLS of the engine's pre-slate E[K] on the board's median posted line. Slope 1.0 = the engine moves with the market. Slope < 1.0 = the engine is over-shrunk toward the mean and will mechanically buy every low line and sell every high line.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.finding: The engine is materially over-shrunk. On the clean, stable subset the slope is 0.703, implying the point projection needs stretching by about 1.42x around its mean.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.why_the_filter_matters: Unfiltered the slope reads 0.426 (stretch 2.35x). The quarantined alt-rung rows alone would have inflated the required correction by roughly 65%. Measuring on dirty rows would have produced a much more aggressive and wrong engine change.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.convergence: This is the SECOND independent measurement pointing the same way. The 7/25 out-of-sample grade gave an OLS slope of actual-on-projected of 1.35 (n=24, outcome-based). This board gives an implied stretch of 1.42 (n=12, market-based). Outcomes and prices are independent yardsticks and they agree on both the direction and roughly the magnitude.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.status: HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING ONLY. Neither measurement was pre-registered. No engine change is licensed by either (R7).
